extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, corporate communicators, and anyone writing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist and style guidance for composing a news-style press release: required components, AP-style dateline formatting, lead/body/boilerplate guidance, and layout/typography rules. Focused on producing a standard, media-ready release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letterhead / logo present
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required component listed first in order. Implicit format checklist: 'Letterhead/logo present' (pass/fail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information (placement and contents)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top right of release. Include name, title, phone (with area code), email, time zone, and available hours. Also include contact URL in boilerplate if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release timing notice
rubrics_metrics.description: "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE" OR "EMBARGOED UNTIL [Date and Time]"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place timing notice top left. Use all caps for 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' or an embargo line 'EMBARGOED UNTIL [Date and Time]'. Aligned to the left.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline formatting and length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should be centered and bold. Checklist: 'Headline centered, bold, ≤100 chars'. Recommended headline font size 14-16pt. Keep within the character limit for clear media use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadline (deck)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a subheadline (deck) under the headline to provide a brief extension or secondary hook. Implicit checklist item: 'Subheadline present.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline AP-style format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dateline format (AP Style): city name in ALL CAPS, state abbreviation (AP-specific, e.g., 'Calif.' not 'CA') when required, date with month spelled out, day as number (no st/nd/th), year; em dash before story. Example: 'WASHINGTON, March 15, 2026 — Acme Corp today announced...'. Major cities stand alone (no state needed) such as NEW YORK, LOS ANGELES, CHICAGO, BOSTON. For international cities, include country if not well-known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph (length and content)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 25-35 words. Answers the 5Ws + H (who, what, when, where, why, how). Most newsworthy information first. Use active voice. One sentence ideal, maximum two sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body paragraphs (structure and order)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3-4 paragraphs typical; each paragraph 1-3 sentences; one idea per paragraph. Use inverted pyramid order (most important information first). Include quotes within the body as specified. Guidance gives a total body length of 400-500 words (see also separate overall length checklist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes (number and attribution)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include 1-2 quotes. Implicit checklist: 'At least one quote with attribution.' Quotes should be attributed to named sources and support or humanize the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate content and placement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final paragraph of the release. Use an 'About [Company]' header. 50-100 words. Write in third person, summarize mission and scope, and include a contact URL. Boilerplate appears at the end of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: End marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '###' centered or '-30-' centered to indicate the release is over.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style throughout
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release should follow AP style conventions consistently (state abbreviations, dateline formatting, dates, capitalization, etc.). Checklist includes 'AP style throughout.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid order
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange information so the most newsworthy facts are first; background and lesser details follow. Listed as a requirement in body paragraph guidance and the implicit checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and grammar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release must be free of spelling and grammar mistakes. Included as an explicit pass/fail checklist item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall length / word count
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit checklist lists 'Length 300-500 words.' Body-paragraph guidance specifies a total of 400-500 words. Note both ranges are provided on the page; aim for concise releases within this approximately 300-500 word window, with body guidance recommending ~400-500 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbers for multi-page releases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include page numbers when the release spans multiple pages (explicit checklist item).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard fonts and typography
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard fonts such as Times, Arial, or Calibri. Body text 10-12pt; headline 14-16pt. These typographic standards are listed in the implicit checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline state abbreviation rules (AP-specific)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AP-specific state abbreviations (e.g., 'Calif.' instead of 'CA'). Major cities stand alone and do not require a state. For international cities, include the country if the city isn't well-known. (This guidance is part of the dateline guidance but also listed as its own subsection.)
